sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bills for a Chattanooga house?
sections.html:
Two governments bill every house inside Chattanooga city limits: Hamilton County and the City of Chattanooga. The Hamilton County Assessor of Property sets the appraisal, the Hamilton County Trustee collects the county bill, and the City Treasurer collects the city bill.

The city says plainly that an owner inside Chattanooga pays both. The Trustee also collects for Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy Daisy and Walden, but not for Chattanooga, so a bill from the Trustee will not cover the city share.

  • Hamilton County Trustee: Room 210 of the Hamilton County Courthouse on Georgia Avenue, plus a satellite office at 6125 Preservation Drive, Suite 101. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Phone (423) 209-7270.
  • City Treasurer: City Hall, 101 E. 11th Street, Room 100. Phone (423) 643-7262 or email ptax@chattanooga.gov.
  • Hamilton County Assessor of Property: (423) 209-7300, for values, mailing address changes and exemption requests.

sections.h2: What dates control a Chattanooga tax bill?
sections.html:
Bills for the year go out in September, taxes are due from October 1, and payment without interest runs through the last day of February. Interest starts on March 1.

The county charges 1.5 percent per month from March 1, which is 18 percent a year. The city describes the same total as 1 percent interest plus a half percent penalty each month. Hamilton County adds that a mailed payment counts as late if the post office does not postmark it in time, while an online payment counts on the day of the transaction.

The bill covers January 1 through December 31 of the tax year. Because taxes are paid in the months after the year they cover, a house that sells in spring may still carry the previous year's bill, and the county tells new owners to read the closing statement to see who owes it.

sections.h2: How is the tax on a Chattanooga house worked out?
sections.html:
The county Assessor sets an appraised value, the state ratio turns that into an assessed value, and each government multiplies the result by its own rate per $100. Chattanooga's page says residential property and farms are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial and industrial property at 40 percent. Properties are reappraised every four years.

As a rough guide, a house appraised at $283,200 would carry an assessed value of $70,800 at the 25 percent ratio, and the city's 1.93 rate would produce a city bill near $1,366 on that value before any county share.

sections.h2: What happens if the tax on a Chattanooga house goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax in Chattanooga becomes a court matter within about a year. The City Treasurer says taxes still unpaid a year after they were due are filed in Hamilton County Chancery Court, and past-due stormwater fees go to a collection agency at the same point.

Once a bill sits in Chancery Court, payment goes to the Clerk and Master at 625 Georgia Avenue, Courthouse Room 300, phone (423) 209-6606, instead of the Treasurer. The city page says a property can be sold for delinquent tax after three years. Hamilton County describes the annual tax sale as held each June, with a one year redemption period afterward.

A stormwater fee rides on the city bill, so a payoff figure should include it. Partial payments post in a set order: stormwater fee interest first, then stormwater fee, then tax interest and penalty, then the tax itself.

sections.h2: How can you pay or look up a Chattanooga tax bill?
sections.html:
Search the parcel on the city's property tax search page, or call the Treasurer for a copy. A missing bill never cancels the due date.

  • Online: card payments carry a 2.55 percent fee with a $2.20 minimum, and e-check carries $2.00. The city keeps none of it.
  • By mail: City Treasurer, P.O. Box 191, Chattanooga, TN 37401-0191, using the original bill with its barcode between October and the end of February.
  • In person: City Hall, Room 100, all year. Full payments are also taken at First Horizon branches in Hamilton County when you bring the original bill.
  • County bill: the Trustee accepts partial payments, and its satellite office at Bonny Oaks handles tax relief appointments.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Chattanooga homeowners?
sections.html:
Chattanooga homeowners who are elderly, disabled, or disabled veterans can apply for state-funded Tax Relief, and a separate Tax Freeze holds the city bill at its qualifying-year amount. One Tax Relief application covers both the city and county bills.

For the 2026 tax year the city lists a combined 2025 income limit of $38,470 for the elderly and disabled categories, and applicants must be 65 by December 31, 2026, or disabled by that date. The maximum reimbursement is $162.12 for those two groups and $844.38 for disabled veterans and their widows or widowers. You must pay the 2026 bill before the application can be processed, and the deadline to apply is April 5, 2027.

Anyone approved for Tax Relief or Tax Freeze can also have the stormwater fee on the current city bill paid through the United Way assistance program. Call (423) 643-7274 for help with the application.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Chattanooga property appraisal?
sections.html:
Start with the Hamilton County Assessor of Property at (423) 209-7300, then go to the Hamilton County Board of Equalization if the talk does not settle it. The Tennessee Comptroller says an assessment generally has to be appealed to the county board to keep later appeal rights.

County boards of equalization normally open on June 1. A further appeal goes to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. Check the current deadline with the Assessor, because the county sets its own filing window.

sections.h2: What is Chattanooga like for a homeowner who needs to sell?
sections.html:
Chattanooga sits along the Tennessee River on the Georgia line, where the ridge-and-valley Appalachians meet the Cumberland Plateau. The city covers about 150 square miles, and the Census Bureau estimated 194,144 residents in July 2025, up from 181,099 at the 2020 count.

Ross's Landing became the city of Chattanooga in 1839, and the railroad arrived in 1850. The largest flood in its history came in 1867, before the Tennessee Valley Authority system existed. Today the economy runs on manufacturing and distribution, including the Volkswagen assembly plant that opened in 2011, plus insurance, health care and BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee on Cameron Hill.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show 79,084 households, a median owner-occupied value of $283,200 and a median gross rent of $1,256. The owner-occupied rate is 52.4 percent, so rental houses are a large share of the stock, which matters for sellers with tenants in place.

sections.h2: How should a seller handle tax due on a Chattanooga house?
sections.html:
Ask the title company for a payoff of every open tax year before closing, and have county, city and stormwater amounts listed separately. Hamilton County states that unpaid taxes continue to accrue against the property, so a balance does not vanish at transfer.

Past-due taxes, interest and any court costs are normally paid from the sale price at closing. If a bill is already with the Clerk and Master, request that office's figure, because it will differ from the Treasurer's. Recording the deed at the Hamilton County Register of Deeds follows the payoff, and the title company usually handles both steps.

faqs.q: When do Chattanooga property taxes become late?
faqs.a: Chattanooga and Hamilton County taxes become late on March 1 after the October 1 due date. From that day each unpaid bill gains 1.5 percent a month, which the county puts at 18 percent a year.

faqs.q: Do I pay Chattanooga city tax and Hamilton County tax separately?
faqs.a: Yes. The City Treasurer bills and collects the city tax, and the Hamilton County Trustee bills and collects the county tax. Paying one does not satisfy the other.

faqs.q: Can I get help paying my Chattanooga property tax bill?
faqs.a: Elderly, disabled and disabled veteran owners can apply for state Tax Relief, and the city also offers a Tax Freeze. The 2026 application deadline is April 5, 2027, and the 2026 bill must be paid first. Call (423) 643-7274 to ask about eligibility.

faqs.q: What if I never received a Chattanooga tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax and the interest. The city and county both say a missing bill does not excuse payment, so look up the parcel on the city's search page or call the Treasurer at (423) 643-7262.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Chattanooga assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Hamilton County Assessor of Property at (423) 209-7300. If the Assessor cannot resolve it, the county Board of Equalization is the next step, and it generally convenes on June 1.
